$comment: Mission 1.66.2 Part F. A support route exists and is published first-party. Mission 1.65 is not made wrong by it.
mission: 1.66.2 — ONYPHE Public Documentation Reconciliation & Configuration-Metadata Closure V1

what_mission_1_65_recorded.$comment: Part F2. Quoted from its own record, and it stays exactly as it is.
what_mission_1_65_recorded.statement: the established recipient is a general contact route published by the provider, and NOT a dedicated technical or support channel. No such channel is published, and this record does not claim one.
what_mission_1_65_recorded.why_it_was_accurate: It described the pages that mission inspected: the about page and the site root. Neither carries a support address.
what_mission_1_65_recorded.why_it_is_not_now_wrong: It is a statement about what those documents establish, not a claim about every page the provider has ever published. A later document extends the evidence; it does not falsify the earlier reading.
what_mission_1_65_recorded.what_would_have_been_wrong: Editing that sentence to say a support channel had been published all along. The mission did not know it, could not have known it from the pages it read, and its record is of what it established.

the_new_first_party_evidence.verbatim_instruction: Do you have any questions? Contact us at support[at]onyphe{dot}io
the_new_first_party_evidence.why_that_matters: A conventional support mailbox is exactly the kind of address a system could guess. This one is not guessed: the provider prints it, three times, beside a sentence telling readers to send questions there.

on_the_printed_form.$comment: Recorded precisely, because this arc has a rule about obfuscated addresses.
on_the_printed_form.why_not: Nothing is being sent, so nothing needs normalising, and the record is more useful holding what the page actually prints.
on_the_printed_form.how_this_differs_from_the_netlas_case: The Netlas address is served through a mechanism that returns a placeholder to automated retrieval, so obtaining it would mean defeating that mechanism. This one was retrieved in full: the page's literal text contains the address in a human-readable typographic form. Reading what a page prints is not circumvention, and the two situations are recorded apart rather than collapsed into one rule.
on_the_printed_form.what_a_future_mission_must_still_do: Establish the recipient under the Mission 1.65 outbound dispatch contract, on its own provenance, before any envelope names it.

what_this_does_not_authorise.$comment: Part F3. The discovery is about future routing and nothing else.
what_this_does_not_authorise.the_existing_dispatch_remains_valid: The enquiry was sent once, on 2026-09-05, to the general contact route the provider publishes on two first-party pages. That route was correctly established and correctly used. A better-targeted route existing does not make the used one wrong, and a second copy of an answered question is a second outbound action requiring its own frozen content and its own approval.

verdict.operational_effect_later: if the general route does not answer, a future mission has a published, provider-designated channel for questions, established rather than guessed
verdict.apparatus_effect: none. A better contact route is not an answer to a methodological question, and no gate moves because a mailbox was found.
